pH
Th e unit for measuring relative acidity or alkalinity of a ﬂ uid
is called pH. Simply stated, pH is the ratio of acids to bases. 
Hydrogen ion concentration (H) is the negative logarithm of 
hydrogen ions in solution:
pH  log 1/[H]  log [H]
Because the scale of (H) is logarithmic, in order for the pH to
change by one unit (e.g., changing from 3 to 4), there must be a
tenfold change in (H).
